newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan army battles Moslem rebels for 10th day.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan army battles Moslem rebels for 10th day.

text.p: Uganda's army battled Moslem rebels who attacked the western town of Bundibugyo from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo for the 10th straight day on Tuesday, a senior army official said.

Lieutenant-Colonel Charles Angina told reporters in the western Ugandan town of Fort Portal that rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) were still putting up resistance around Bundibugyo and the road leading into the small town remained closed.

Angina, who is involved in the operations against the rebels, estimated the rebel force at around 1,300 and said they were sponsored by neighbouring Sudan with the sole intention of destabilising President Yoweri Museveni's government.
"It has more to do with the Sudan. The weapons and mines for these people have come from the Sudan through Zaire. It is about destabilising Museveni and his regime," Angina added.

U.N. officials in Fort Portal said a World Food Programme convoy to deliver food to some 20,000 internally displaced people in Bundibugyo failed to leave because of insecurity on the Fort Portal-Bundibugyo road.
WFP officials in the Kenyan capital Nairobi said the agency was to deliver up to 60 tonnes of emergency aid.
"They will give it another try on Wednesday," an aid official in Fort Portal told Reuters.
On Monday, Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi told Reuters that the rebel force had broken into small groups and attacked the town with mortars and the army was fighting to repulse them.

The government-owned New Vision newspaper reported on Monday that up to 300 rebels took part in the attack on Bundibugyo and at least 20 soldiers had been wounded and taken to hospital after the attacks.
Officials say between 15,000 and 20,000 people have been displaced by the fighting and have fled into Bundibugyo from surrounding areas.
